newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FORECAST-Consensus of RBNZ economic projections.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Consensus of RBNZ economic projections.

text.p: Following is a survey of economists' expectations for the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's economic projections due on Thursday, March 13.
We asked economists whether they expected the Reserve Bank on Thursday to signal:
(b) implicitly an easing in monetary conditions;
or (e) to urge financial markets to hold conditions steady.
Following are their responses and comments:
ANZ BANK: (e). "Further slight easing in coming months contingent upon further evidence of easing inflationary pressures."
ASB BANK: (b). "Conditions currently tighter than likely 'preferred conditions'."
BANCORP TREASURY SERVICES: (e). "There is room for a slight easing in conditions in the June quarter, however the risks to this are many, so the probability of it eventuating remains low."

BANKERS TRUST: Did not choose an option from the above list. "We think the RBNZ's assumed mix will be somewhat easier than where the market is today. However, it will be the same overall mix as assumed in the December (monetary policy) statement. We see the RBNZ tightening by the middle of 1997."
CAVILL WHITE SECURITIES: (d). "Expect RB to remain uncomfortable with inflationary expectations in private sector and underlying (inflation) close to top end of 0-3 pct band."

DEUTSCHE MORGAN GRENFELL: (b) if conditions stay at today's levels. "If they fall back to 2:1 line (where the RBNZ said a 2 percent move in the currency index approximately offset a one percentage point move in 90-day bank bills) beforehand, then (e) applies."
DOYLE PATERSON BROWN: (b). Current conditions are now 100 basis points tighther than the RB's December optimal. This is probably unnecessary."
FIRST NZ CAPITAL: (d). "The market has done much of the tightening for them."
SBC WARBURG: (e). "But the inflation forecasts will suggest a bias to (b). Possibly the next explicit action will be to tighten by end-1997."
We asked economists to state what they thought the RBNZ would forecast for growth in production-based GDP (March quarter to March quarter) in the following years.
UNDERLYING INFLATION, TWI AND 90-DAY BANK BILL ASSUMPTIONS

We asked economists to state what they thought the RBNZ's forecasts will be for March quarter to March quarter changes in underlying inflation; the rate of appreciation the bank will assume in the New Zealand dollar Trade-Weighted Index, and the starting point it will take for the index; and the bank's technical assumption for 90-day bank bill rates over its forecast period.
* BTNZ said there was a chance oil prices were removed for the March 1997 quarter. If so, the RBNZ would indicate that in the forecasts.

** WestpacTrust said that in addition to these 90-day bank bill and TWI assumptions, the Reserve Bank would assume the same 2:1 trade-off between the two that it detailed in the December monetary policy statement.
